Article Title: Five minutes, 28 covers, 300 tyres: How Galle's 130-member groundstaff beat the rain
Article Text:
A view of the covered pitch and ground on Day 2 of the first Test match between India and Sri Lanka at the Galle International Cricket Stadium. (ANI)

TimesofIndia.com in Galle:

Manjula watching the proceedings at the Galle International Stadium. (Photo Courtesy: Sahil Malhotra)

We keep our eyes on the ocean. When clouds start building up, we know it's coming. Then we are ready and wait for the official signal to start covering the pitch, square, run-up and then the entire ground. Manjula | Groundsmen at Galle International Stadium

Groundsmen of Galle International Stadium in action. (Photo Courtesy: Sahil Malhotra)

Galle [Sri Lanka], Aug 15 (ANI): Ground staff cover the ground as it rains during day 1 of the 1st Test match between Sri Lanka and India, in Galle on Saturday. (ANI Photo)

The match was over. The formalities were completed, and both teams had already left the stadium. The broadcast crew was busy packing up for the next game, but the work was only getting started for Manjula and the 130 groundstaff at the Galle International Cricket Stadium. It rained immediately after the two teams completed their handshakes, but unlike the preceding week, there was no urgency to cover the square or the ground. Overseeing operations, Manjula stood on top of the advertising board and kept a close eye as the covers were neatly folded and parked after a week of intense activity.Since India and Sri Lanka arrived in the coastal city for the series opener, rain has appeared frequently enough to keep Manjula and his team on their toes. Not all of them are employees of Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC). Only 16 are permanent staff in Galle, while 10 came from Hambantota to help with the international fixture. The remaining staff were hired as daily workers."We have 16 permanent employees and 10 come from Hambantota whenever an international match comes to Galle. For the rest, we hire daily workers for the duration of the match and practice sessions, and they are paid between 2,500 LKR and 4,000 LKR per day for the work," says Manjula.From anticipation to execution, the groundstaff stuck to their methods and ensured there was no chaos, even during a heavy downpour. The average time they take to cover the entire ground is less than five minutes, and they work quickly depending on the situation. They look for cues, observe the cloud behaviour and are always staring towards the Indian Ocean near the Galle Fort."We keep our eyes there," he says, pointing towards the ocean near the fort. "When clouds start building up, we know it's coming. Then we are ready and wait for the official signal to start covering the pitch, square, run-up and then the entire ground. That's the order we follow.""The reaction time is very important," he adds.When the groundstaff run from all directions, dragging the covers, the synchronised effort is a sight. The first batch, covering the pitch and square, times their runs so there is no overlapping, and speed cannot be compromised because the run-up and the remainder of the field must be covered next. These are anything but light covers, and a 100x100 piece can weigh over 650 kg. Add to this the challenges of wind and rain."These are not light," Manjula says with a laugh. "They are well over 650 kg each for a 100x100 piece, and there are about 28 pieces we have to cover the entire ground and ensure no damage is done to the outfield."While the covers are heavy enough to stay grounded on their own, heavy crosswinds present a challenge, and the next step is to carefully place heavy rubber tyres to keep the covers in place. More than 300 tyres are ready to be rolled onto the ground the moment rain arrives."We keep these tyres over the covers because, as you have seen, it does get very windy. All this has to happen within a few minutes because the ground can't be exposed for a long time. Sometimes showers are short but very strong. So reaction is key," explains Manjula while pointing towards the tyres placed behind the LED boards.Removing the covers is also a work of art. They are not recklessly peeled off but carefully rolled out with enough waves to ensure water is deposited near the ropes and doesn't spill onto the field.In addition to the groundstaff and their incredible performance, the Galle International Stadium has four functional Super Soppers that work their magic the moment the rain stops and the outfield needs preparation for resumption. In the last week, all the pieces came together seamlessly, and the field showed no sign of interruption.Most will be without work from Thursday, and some will travel back to Hambantota, but their relentless efforts deserve applause as they ensured crucial time wasn't lost.
Article Summary: Groundstaff at the Galle International Cricket Stadium cover the pitch, square, run-up and then the entire ground in less than five minutes. Only 16 are permanent staff in Galle, while 10 came from Hambantota to help with the international fixture. The remaining staff were hired as daily workers.

Article Title: Delhi’s invisible opponent: How drift is becoming a factor at the World Championships
Article Text:
New Delhi: USA's Garret Tan being attended by a physio after an injury (PTI Photo)

New Delhi:

Box Items:

WHAT'S DRIFT?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

H

OW DRIFT CHANGES THE GAME

In a sport decided by precision and where the smallest margins can separate a winner from a loser, the most talked-about variable at the Indira Gandhi (IG) indoor stadium is something players cannot see. It is the air.At the BWF World Championships , the much-discussed “drift” has emerged as an additional tactical challenge, compelling shuttlers to recalibrate their strokes, movement and shot selection almost from rally to rally. With air-conditioning and ventilation creating differing currents across the arena, the four courts are not playing alike — and even the two ends of the same court can demand different solutions.The effect is most pronounced on Centre Court 1 and adjacent Court 3, where airflow from the AC vents creates noticeable side drift. Court 2 has also shown some movement, though comparatively less troublesome, while Court 4, farther from the strongest vents, has remained largely stable.For players, that difference can be decisive. Lakshya Sen experienced it immediately in his opening-round victory over Austria’s Collins Valentine Filimon. The Indian struggled to find his range early, particularly with delicate net play, before shrinking his stroke production and bringing Filimon into longer exchanges."I adapted after the change of ends, opened up the rallies and stopped playing the short, flat exchanges that had initially allowed him (Filimon) to dictate," Sen had said after his win. The conditions, however, were not the sole reason for Sen's defeat to American Garret Tan on Wednesday.Kodai Naraoka’s assessment was even more revealing. In his three-game victory over Chi Yu Jen, the Japanese shuttler found one half markedly quicker while the opposite side appeared to hold the shuttle back. The contrast was stark enough to contribute to a 21-12, 7-21, 21-16 scoreline. "The side opposite to the audience was the fast one. On the other hand, the shuttle was not travelling for me. It was sometimes stopping before I could reach the net," Naraoka said.Ayush Shetty’s headline-making upset of world No. 1 and defending champion Shi Yu Qi was also a case in point. Shetty prevailed 21-14, 13-21, 21-19, but the Chinese star repeatedly appeared uncomfortable when playing from the more difficult end on the Centre Court, particularly while lifting the shuttle.Coach Vimal Kumar felt the drift affected Shi’s judgement and timing, especially when he had to send the shuttle high and deep. "The challenge in drifty conditions is that once the shuttle is in the air, it can float unpredictably, making it difficult to make the perfect connection when attacking, especially on the smash," he explained.Canadian Victor Lai described the shuttle as unusually floaty and said players had to shorten their swings, sharpen their strokes and be wary of cross-court shots being carried beyond the lines. "...Got used to the conditions a bit better. One side there’s drift: one side is slower and one side’s faster. The side drift’s not crazy strong, but still a little bit. The wind blows the shuttle very strong. But honestly, I have kind of gotten used to it a lot of places like this, China, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand too, a lot of these Asian countries have this sort of drift. I won’t say like I am perfect, but I am getting used to it," he told BWF media.The drift has also been part of the backdrop to Indian losses on Court 3, including men's doubles pair M R Arjun and H Amsakarunan’s defeat to South Korea’s M H Kang and D Ki. Unnati Hooda, who pushed Michelle Li to 23-21 in the decider, also saw crucial side pushes drift beyond the lines."It was for both (the drift). We have to adjust to conditions as players. I thought of switching to flick serves but then didn't do it," Unnati said.While badminton remains a game of skill, nerve, execution and tactics, but in Delhi, players are discovering that mastering the air is equally important.Drift is the sideways or directional movement of air inside an indoor badminton hall. Unlike outdoor wind, it is generated by ventilation, air-conditioning, temperature differences, humidity, doors opening and closing, and even crowd movement.When the shuttle enters a moving air current, its trajectory can change subtly but significantly.A shuttle travelling with the airflow can move faster or carry deeper; against it, the same stroke may slow, dip or fall short. Cross-drift can push flat shots and lifts sideways. Players therefore alter racket speed, swing length, smash power, lift height and positioning. The result is a constant process of recalibration — especially when changing ends, where the same shot may require a completely different touch.
Article Summary: Air-conditioning and ventilation create differing currents across the arena. Effect is most pronounced on Centre Court 1 and adjacent Court 3. Court 4, farther from the strongest vents, has remained largely stable. Lakshya Sen experienced it immediately in his opening-round victory.

Article Title: Rain, rust and neglect: Javelin machine bought with medal ambitions lies unused at JLN stadium
Article Text:
Javelin machine

New Delhi:

Javelin machine lies neglected

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A specialised javelin-throwing machine that was procured to sharpen India’s elite throwing edge is lying unused in the open at Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) stadium, exposed to Delhi’s monsoon after months without installation.visited the stadium premises on Tuesday afternoon and found the equipment behind the boys’ sports hostel/residential complex, wrapped in polythene, lying uninstalled and gathering dust, moisture and grime. People familiar with the matter said the machine's procurement was approved in Jan 2026 and has remained unused since its arrival in March, with no space earmarked for its proper set-up.sent a detailed questionnaire on Tuesday evening through official email channels to the sports ministry, Sports Authority of India (SAI), its director general and TOPS headquarters. The queries sought responses on procurement, cost, intended use, non-installation, and exposure to the monsoon.Responses were also sought on what safeguards were in place for the machine’s computer, sensors and other components against rain, moisture, dust and rust, and whether any damage had been assessed. At the time of publication, responses were awaited. The story will be updated if replies are received.According to sources, the machine cost around Rs 15 lakh and was procured under the govt’s 'Make in India' initiative for advanced javelin-specific strength training. The sources added that a Mission Olympic Cell (MOC) proposal worth Rs 22 lakh was cleared for leading javelin thrower Sachin Yadav’s training and equipment requirements for major competitions in 2026, including the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow and the Asian Games.Wrapped in polythene, the machine has reportedly never been installed even once. There is no earmarked outdoor space, sources said, leaving the costly apparatus exposed to weather damage.The apparatus is modelled on the German Kraft Trainings Gerät (KTG), a specialised strength-training system associated with elite German throwers, including legendary Uwe Hohn. The concept uses a weighted sled to replicate the explosive upward drive required in javelin throwing, helping athletes develop sport-specific power and release speed.The machine has a 3.8kg sled that can accommodate up to 10kg of additional weight, taking the total load to 13.8kg. Its resistance and movement are designed to enable athletes to repeatedly train the throwing action at specific release angles. The equipment also incorporates electronic components, including a computer and sensors, to provide training feedback.The technology was made famous by German throwers and was also used in China before India acquired a locally manufactured and adapted version. India became the third country to procure such a javelin-specific machine. Its acquisition was seen as another step towards building high-end indigenous sports equipment.A similar KTG-type machine had been installed at the National Institute of Sports, Patiala, ahead of the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, allowing Neeraj Chopra and other javelin throwers to train on the specialised apparatus.At JLN stadium, however, the equipment has remained outside. Sources said the lack of an earmarked installation area prevented its use, even though several elite, emerging and talented javelin throwers train at the facility. The machine, sources said, could have benefitted throwers preparing for major competitions, besides younger athletes seeking specialised strength training.
Article Summary: Specialised javelin-throwing machine lying unused in the open at Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) stadium, exposed to Delhi’s monsoon after months without installation. The machine cost around Rs 15 lakh and was procured under the govt's 'Make in India' initiative. The apparatus is modelled on the German Kraft Trainings Gerät.

Article Title: Navneet Kaur’s experience could hold key against England
Article Text:
Navneet Kaur

TOI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Years of experience have taught Navneet Kaur something that cannot be picked up in training — how to find the balance between staying composed and knowing when to be aggressive.That balance could be crucial when the Indian women’s hockey team faces England in their final Pool D game on Thursday, with a draw enough to take them into the next round.The India forward — who has more than 200 senior international caps for India — has been one of the standout performers for the Indian women’s team this year. After leading SG Pipers to victory in the Women’s Hockey India League (HIL), Navneet was India’s leading scorer in the World Cup qualifiers in Hyderabad, where her four goals helped the hosts finish runners-up and book their place at the World Cup.She carried that form into the Nations Cup in New Zealand, scoring another four goals, and has shown no signs of slowing down at the World Cup.The 30-year-old has found the net in both of India’s matches so far, scoring against China and South Africa, while also creating chances and making intelligent runs to underline her importance to the team’s attack. Against England, who got the better of India when the two teams met in the World Cup qualifiers, her ability to make the right decisions in the attacking third will once again prove crucial.“When you are younger, you feel differently. You are a little more nervous and think about how things will happen. But now, with experience, you understand what you need to do, how to keep yourself composed during a match and when you need to be more aggressive,” Navneet toldThat understanding, she feels, has come with years of playing at the highest level.“I have found that balance with experience. You learn how to focus on yourself while also taking your teammates along with you, and you understand the responsibility that comes with being a senior player,” she said.There is also an added responsibility this time. With 11 players in India’s squad playing their first World Cup — including two teenagers — Navneet is among those expected to help the newcomers settle into the biggest stage.“Of course, there is a responsibility as a senior player. But when young players come into the team, they also bring a different kind of energy. They can bring more energy and cover a lot of ground,” said Navneet, who also played alongside several of these players during the HIL.For Navneet, the key is making sure the youngsters feel comfortable enough to speak up, particularly if they are nervous about playing at a World Cup. Interestingly, she also sees the team’s relative inexperience as a potential advantage. While opponents have studied India’s established players over the years, the newcomers are less familiar to them.“Teams study us through videos and they know what the senior players usually do, but they may not know as much about the youngsters. That can also be an advantage for us,” she said.India’s campaign has already given the youngsters valuable exposure, but the team’s extensive match experience this year will also be important when they take on England. India have had a busy build-up, playing two tournaments as well as friendly series against Argentina and Australia and practice matches against Germany and the Netherlands among others.“The more matches we play against different teams, the better our understanding of the game becomes,” she said. “When we play actual matches, different scenarios come up. We can then discuss those situations, watch the videos and find solutions to them.”That experience will now come into focus against England, with India knowing that a draw would be enough to take them into the next round. For a player who has grown into one of India’s key attacking figures, Thursday’s game offers another opportunity for Navneet’s experience, composure and attacking instinct to make a difference.
Article Summary: Navneet Kaur has more than 200 senior international caps for India. The 30-year- old has been one of the standout performers for the Indian women’s team this year. India face England in their final Pool D game on Thursday, with a draw enough to take them into the next round.

Article Title: BWF World Championships: Lakshya Sen fights back to down Austria's Collins Filimon
Article Text:
Lakshya Sen

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: For 21 minutes at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium here, Lakshya Sen found himself locked in an uncomfortable tussle against an invisible adversary. Faced with some tricky court conditions, where the drift made shot-making a guessing game, Lakshya initially looked unsettled against Austria's Collins Valentine Filimon. His strokes were not finding their intended targets, his timing was off and the Austrian made the most of Lakshya's discomfort to pocket the opening game.But Lakshya, who has built his game around patience, movement and the ability to stay in a rally long enough, didn't panic. On Tuesday, that temperament came to the fore as the Indian turned a difficult opening into a commanding 16-21, 21-8, 21-4 victory in 45 minutes in the first round of the ongoing BWF World Championships The transformation was striking. From being tentative and unable to control the shuttle on the windy side of the court, Lakshya gradually began to dictate the terms. He slowed the exchanges down, engaged Filimon in longer rallies and stopped trying to force the pace with sheer power.As the second game progressed, Lakshya began to look increasingly assured. His footwork became sharper, his defensive retrievals more purposeful and his strokes began to open up the court.Once he found his rhythm, Filimon had few answers.The second and third games were not merely a reflection of Lakshya's superior shot-making. It was also a statement of his mental reset. Once he understood how the drift was behaving, he stopped fighting the court and started using it as part of his strategy. If Lakshya's comeback was built on experience and adjustment, Unnati Hooda's women's singles opening-round win was an exercise in composure.The 18-year-old had to navigate her own share of nerves and uncertainty against Myanmar's Thet Htar Thuzar. The opening game was a tight contest, with neither player willing to give much away. Unnati edged it 22-20 and then found enough control to close out the second 21-16, completing a 40-minute victory.For India, the day also brought a mixed bag across the doubles draws. Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand beat 16th seeded American pair of Lauren Lam and Allison Quynh Lee 21-15, 21-12 in 39 minutes and advance to the pre-quarterfinals.Kavipriya Selvam and Simran Singhi, however, were beaten 7-21, 14-21 by Bulgarian sisters Gabriela Stoeva and Stefani Stoeva in 39 minutes.In mixed doubles, Ashith Surya and Amruth Pramuthesh were involved in one of the day's longest battles before going down to Turkey's Emre Sonmez and Yasemen Bektas 21-16, 29-30, 22-24 in 71 minutes. Rohan Kapoor and Ruthvika Shivani Gadde also bowed out after a spirited fight against Canada's Jonathan Lai and Crystal Lai, losing 22-20, 19-21, 17-21 in 68 minutes.
Article Summary: Lakshya Sen turned a difficult opening into a commanding 16-21, 21-8,. 21-4 victory in 45 minutes. Unnati Hooda's women's singles win was an exercise in composure. Ashith Surya and Amruth Pramuthesh were involved in one of the day's longest battles before going down to Turkey's Emre Sonmez.

Article Title: Hockey pioneer Lalremsiami, first in football-mad Mizoram, to win Arjuna Award
Article Text:
Lalremsiami

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kolkata: Indian women’s hockey international Lalremsiami became the first athlete from Mizoram to be selected for the prestigious Arjuna Award after the list for 2025 was unveiled by the sports ministry on Tuesday.Having made her senior debut in 2017, the 26-year-old has been a mainstay of the national team, playing a pivotal role in major tournaments, including India’s fourth-place finish at the Tokyo Olympics under coach Sjoerd Marijne. She was also named FIH Rising Star of the Year in 2019.As recently as the Nations Cup in June, Siami produced a player-of-the-match performance in the final as India beat New Zealand. She will have to continue her good form if India are to make a deep run at the ongoing World Cup.Perhaps happiest to see Lalremsiami selected for the Arjuna was her long-time coach, Miss B’tei, who trained her during her early days at SAI Training Centre in Thenzawl.“I identified her potential and believed that she would one day represent the country. She is a very hardworking and dedicated athlete, I am extremely proud of her performance on such a big world stage,” coach B’tei told TOI.“Now, she will become an inspiration for the younger generation.Seeing Siami receive this award will make children believe that they too can achieve great things. It will give them tremendous encouragement and determination to pursue their dreams,” she added.Siami’s rise to the national team has already made a difference in football-mad Mizoram, with several youngsters taking up hockey and subsequently making their way to National Centres of Excellence (NCOEs) across the country in recent years.Lalthantluangi recently became the third player from the state to make the women’s national team and is currently part of India’s World Cup squad.Mizoram sports minister Lalnghinglova Hmar believes even better days are in store for the sport following Lalremsiami’s historic honour.“This recognition will undoubtedly inspire many Mizo boys and girls to take up sport, dream big and aim for greater achievements. Siami is a role model both on and off the pitch, and an inspiration to countless young Mizos. Heartiest congratulations to Lalremsiami and the entire hockey fraternity of Mizoram. This is a proud moment for all of us,” Hmar told TOI.The Mizoram government has already identified hockey as one of the priority sports under its Empowering Mizoram Sports scheme, and Hmar believes Lalremsiami’s achievement will further promote the game in the state.For now, however, celebrations will have to wait for Lalremsiami. With India’s World Cup campaign underway, there is perhaps nothing she would like more than to make her mark on the biggest stage.
Article Summary: Lalremsiami is the first athlete from Mizoram to be selected for the prestigious Arjuna Award. The 26-year-old made her senior debut in 2017 and has been a mainstay of the national team. She was also named FIH Rising Star of the Year in 2019.

Article Title: India romp past South Africa to register biggest win in Women's Hockey World Cup history
Article Text:
Photo/Agencies

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

“Keep pushing and keep motivating each other!” Former India captain and goalkeeper Savita could be heard above the din, telling the India huddle exactly what needed to be done ahead of their World Cup match against South Africa.And they did just that. India romped to a 6-1 win in their second group game in Amstelveen on Tuesday — their biggest win in World Cup history.Knowing they needed a big win, Sjoerd Marijne’s side came out all guns blazing, looking for goals from the word go. However, it was South Africa who had the first shot on goal within minutes, and for a moment, it seemed things might not be as easy for India.But Bichu Devi Kharibam made a good save to settle India’s nerves, and after a few near misses, the onslaught began.Sunelita Toppo (11), Navneet Kaur (17), Sushila Chanu Pukhrambam (25), Deepika (38), Lalremsiami (44) and Sakshi Rana (45) scored the goals as India went top of Group D with four points. China, who beat England 4-2 in the other group game earlier, also have four points, but India have a better goal difference.Towards the end, South Africa did find the net when Kayla de Waal scored following a penalty corner, but by then India knew the job was done.All focus now moves to Thursday when India take on England. A win or a draw there will take them through to the next round, irrespective of what happens in the match between China and South Africa.Despite Tuesday’s big win, however, it wasn’t a great game from India’s point of view, particularly in the first half when they were sloppy at times. Too many mis-passes and poor first touches could have been costly and India were fortunate that South Africa did not take advantage of them.Speaking during the half-time break, Marijne told the broadcaster: “Of course, when you see the score, you can say we are happy with 3-0, but I think it can be more. And I expect more from the team as well.”“We’ve seen too many individual errors, and they have had some good opportunities. So that’s something we really need to do better. Hopefully, we can score some more goals. That would be great,” he added.In the end, they did score more goals in the third quarter before taking their foot off the pedal in the fourth, when South Africa finally got a breakthrough of their own.The India players, meanwhile, were particularly good inside the D with their short passing. Both their opener and Deepika’s goal came from such moves. Navneet also continued her good showing, as did Neha, and Navneet was more than pleased with six different players finding the net.“If you see, six of our players scored goals, so it’s nice and feels good. Everyone in our team can score, and that’s good for us,” Navneet said after the game.Six different players getting on the scoresheet was perhaps the clearest reflection of the togetherness Marijne has been demanding from his side. The red-and-yellow ‘unity bands’ that every player and support staff member has been wearing around their wrists for the World Cup are meant to represent that spirit.On Tuesday, India showed that unity on the pitch as well.Yet the first-half performance also showed why Marijne wants more from his team. Against England on Thursday, India will need not just the goals but also greater control, discipline and precision if they are to take the next step in their World Cup campaign.
Article Summary: India beat South Africa 6-1 in their second World Cup game on Tuesday. Sunelita Toppo, Navneet Kaur, Sushila Chanu Pukhrambam, Deepika, Lalremsiami and Sakshi Rana scored the goals. Sjoerd Marijne's side go top of Group D with four points.

Article Title: Chaos! Daniil Medvedev loses cool, breaks two advertising boards at Cincinnati Open - Watch
Article Text:
Daniil Medvedev loses cool (Screengrabs)

Missed chances spark meltdown

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Frustration boils over

Daniil Medvedev endured a dramatic night at the Cincinnati Open, missing three match points before losing 6-7(3), 7-6(4), 6-1 to Brandon Nakashima.The Russian also damaged advertising boards, knocked over microphones and argued with the umpire during a frustrating third-round defeat.Medvedev had to fight hard to win the first set after Nakashima led 5-2 and had chances to close it out. He recovered and took the tiebreak, but the second set slipped away despite Medvedev having three match points.Nakashima saved all three chances and levelled the match at 5-5. Frustrated, Medvedev threw his racket into an advertising board, damaging it.Later in the tiebreak, he kicked another board twice after falling 4-2 behind. Umpire Mohamed Lahyani responded with a code violation.The situation became worse in the deciding set as Nakashima quickly moved into a 3-1 lead and then extended it to 5-1. Medvedev's frustration boiled over again as he kicked a microphone before knocking it down.After it was replaced, he knocked it over once more and then dragged another microphone to the ground with his hands.Medvedev eventually lost the match and exited Cincinnati in the third round. The result continues a difficult run at the tournament, where he has failed to reach the fourth round in his last four appearances.Nakashima, who recently reached the Canadian Open final, advances to face Nuno Borges as he targets another Masters 1000 quarter-final.
Article Summary: Daniil Medvedev lost 6-7(3), 7-6(4), 6-1 to Brandon Nakashima. The Russian also damaged advertising boards, knocked over microphones and argued with the umpire during a frustrating third-round defeat. He has failed to reach the fourth round in his last four appearances.

Article Title: Existing selection panel to finalize Rajasthan Ranji Trophy squad
Article Text:
Ranji Trophy gets underway on Oct 11, and the Under-23 CK Nayudu Trophy rounds out the lineup when it begins on Oct 12.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jaipur: With a packed domestic season fast approaching, Rajasthan Cricket Association (RCA) finds itself in a race against time to assemble its squads. A quick succession of four major BCCI domestic tournaments starting in October has pushed selection matters to the forefront.The action begins on Oct 8 with the Boys Under-19 Vinoo Mankad Trophy, followed closely by the Women’s Under-19 T2o Trophy starting on Oct 9. The marquee Ranji Trophy gets underway on Oct 11, and the Under-23 CK Nayudu Trophy rounds out the lineup when it begins on October 12.Insiders share that Bhaskar A Sawant, appointed by the high court as the sole administrator to manage the state cricket affairs, is sticking with the selection panel formed by the last ad hoc committee. Forming new committees would require an Annual General Meeting (AGM) to be convened, which is deemed too demanding a task given that preparations for the upcoming elections must also be attended to.“The five-member panel formed by the last ad hoc committee will be the sole authority to pick the squad. The selectors are scheduled to meet on Thursday to finalise the Ranji Trophy probable list,” a source informed.The senior men’s selection committee formed in June is led by chairperson Vijendra Yadav and includes panel members Zakir Hussain, Shamsher Singh, Pranay Sharma and Afroz Khan.Another source added, “Some players are concerned about how the selection process will unfold because this committee wasn’t formed when the league matches of the Colvin Shield Trophy were going on. Will the five observers from that time be consulted?”Oversight during the Colvin Shield was managed by observers Siddharth Joshi, Ankit Lamba, Abhijeet Sharma, Rajiv Rathore, Pranay Sharma, Kishan Choudhary and Sumit Mathur.Meanwhile, Under-19 Dungarpur Shield will begin on Aug 22.

Article Title: Manav Suthar, Devdutt Padikkal strengthen case as India’s next long-term Test assets
Article Text:
Devdutt Padikkal and Manav Suthar (Agency Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s crushing victory over Sri Lanka in the first Test in Galle unearthed two potential long-term assets in different departments — left-arm spinner Manav Suthar and batter Devdutt Padikkal.Suthar, in particular, looks every bit a Test star in the making. In just two Tests, the 24-year-old has claimed 17 wickets at an average of 11.35, including two five-wicket hauls and his maiden 10-wicket match haul. In Galle, he showcased the classical virtues of left-arm spin, extracting loop, drift, turn and bounce.Padikkal, meanwhile, grabbed his opportunity with both hands. Playing his first Test in 19 months after replacing the injured Sai Sudharsan at No. 3, the stylish left-hander marked his return with a majestic 167, the standout innings of the match, followed by a useful 44 in the second innings. Comfortable against spin on both the front and back foot, Padikkal has strengthened his case to retain the No. 3 slot.Suthar made an impact from his very first ball, trapping Dinesh Chandimal with a beauty that pitched, bounced and turned away before finding the edge to Rishabh Pant.On the final day, he wrapped up Sri Lanka’s tail with smart variations in pace and an effective straighter delivery.Former India left-arm spinner and selector Venkatapathy Raju believes familiarity with subcontinental conditions and a recent county stint with Warwickshire have played a key role in Suthar’s rapid rise. The youngster took 11 wickets in two county matches, including a maiden five-for against Somerset.“I was very impressed by Suthar’s attitude. He has a high-arm action, bowls close to the wicket and possesses the aggression needed to succeed as a left-arm spinner. Playing his first two Tests in familiar conditions has helped, while county cricket gave him valuable red-ball experience,” Raju told TOI.“This will do wonders for his confidence. He can bowl long spells, challenge both right-handers and left-handers and has shown all the signs of becoming a very good bowler.”India vice-captain KL Rahul credited Suthar’s accuracy, subtle changes in pace and ability to exploit drift for making him such a potent threat.“It’s the subtle variations from the same action and angle. He can bowl slower or quicker without changing his arm speed. In Galle, he used the wind beautifully to get drift before the ball either straightened or came back in,” Rahul said.Rahul also praised Suthar’s consistency in hitting the right areas.“His greatest strength is his pace through the air and his ability to challenge every mode of dismissal. The line he bowls brings LBW into play, while any turn can produce catches behind. That’s a special skill.”The vice-captain was equally effusive about Padikkal, with whom he shared a 150-run partnership in the first innings.“That innings defined the Test,” Rahul said. “The tempo he batted at and the fact that he converted it into a big hundred really set the game up for us. The conditions were physically demanding, so to get his first Test hundred and go on to score big was special. I’ve watched him grow through Karnataka cricket and it was wonderful to witness his first Test hundred.”
Article Summary: Manav Suthar and Devdutt Padikkal starred in India's crushing victory over Sri Lanka in the first Test in Galle. The 24-year-old left-arm spinner has claimed 17 wickets at an average of 11.35 in just two Tests, including two five-wicket hauls and his maiden 10- wicket match haul. The stylish left-hander marked his return with a majestic 167, the standout innings of the match, and a useful 44 in the second innings.

Article Title: Manav Suthar spins India to 165-run win, seals historic victory in Galle
Article Text:
Galle: India's Manav Suthar, with teammates celebrates after taking a wicket (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Talk about arriving in Test cricket with a bang. Just minutes after Manav Suthar bowled debutant Keshara Nuwantha to seal India’s emphatic 165-run win over Sri Lanka in the first Test at the Galle International Cricket Stadium, heavy rain lashed the venue.By then, however, the damage had been done, with the young left-arm spinner delivering a performance for the ages.Suthar ripped through Sri Lanka’s lower order in a sensational spell. In the 76th over, he bowled a three-wicket maiden, dismissing the resolute Sonal Dinusha (84; 128b, 8x4, 1x6), who was caught at leg slip by Dhruv Jurel, before removing Prabhat Jayasuriya for a duck off the very next ball. Though he missed out on a hat-trick, Suthar completed his second five-wicket haul in Test cricket by having Lahiru Kumara caught behind.His late burst earned him figures of 6-55 in 23.4 overs as Sri Lanka were dismissed for 206 in 77.4 overs while chasing an improbable 372. The 24-year-old finished with match figures of 10/131 in 45.2 overs after taking 4-76 in the first innings, making him the undisputed architect of India’s victory and making the team’s 600th Test memorable.The victory also kept India firmly in contention for a place in the 2027 World Test Championship final.They remain fifth in the standings but improved their points percentage to 53.33 while Sri Lanka stayed sixth on 33.33. Australia currently lead the table, followed by South Africa. With one match left in the series, Sri Lanka can no longer win it but will aim to deny India a series victory in the second Test beginning on Sunday.Chasing what would have been the highest successful fourth-innings total in Galle, Sri Lanka never threatened after beginning the final day at 84-4. While Suthar dominated proceedings, pacer Prasidh Krishna also played a key role, producing a fiery spell to finish with 2-16 from 10 overs.Prasidh’s second wicket came after an intriguing exchange involving Niroshan Dickwella. Amid constant chatter from Yashasvi Jaiswal , who challenged him to play the hook shot and jokingly suggested he could recommend him to his IPL coach Kumar Sangakkara, Dickwella appeared distracted.Attempting an ambitious stroke after backing away from the stumps, the left-hander top-edged to wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant and departed for 10.Kuldeep Yadav, meanwhile, looked off-colour, returning figures of 1/38 from 11 overs, which could prompt discussions about giving rookie off-spinner Saransh Jain an opportunity in Colombo.
Article Summary: India beat Sri Lanka by 165 runs in the first Test at the Galle International Cricket Stadium. Manav Suthar took 6-55 as Sri Lanka were dismissed for 206 in 77.4 overs while chasing an improbable 372. The 24-year-old finished with match figures of 10/131 in 45.2 overs.

Article Title: Manav Suthar scripts history, equals 93-year-old record after stunning Sri Lanka Test show
Article Text:
Galle: India's Manav Suthar, centre, celebrates (PTI Photo(

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Manav Suthar scripted a remarkable piece of Indian Test history on Wednesday (August 19), becoming the first spinner and only the second Indian cricketer to claim a five-wicket haul in both his first home and first away Tests.The 24-year-old Rajasthan spinner had announced himself on the international stage on his Test debut against Afghanistan in Mullanpur on June 6, 2026, taking six wickets in the first innings. He continued his impressive start on his first overseas assignment against Sri Lanka in Galle, where he finished with 10 wickets across the Test played from August 15 to 19.Suthar returned figures of 4 for 76 in Sri Lanka's first innings before producing a match-defining spell in the second innings. He picked up six wickets for just 55 runs as India completed a 165-run victory.His achievement puts him in an exclusive club that previously had only one member.Mohammad Nisar was the first Indian to accomplish the feat. Nisar made his Test debut against England at Lord's on June 25, 1932, and took 5 for 93 in the first innings. He went on to become the first Indian bowler to claim a five-wicket haul in Test cricket.Nisar's first home Test came against England in Mumbai from December 15, 1933.He again produced a five-wicket haul, finishing with 5 for 90 in the first innings.For 94 years, no other Indian had managed to take five wickets in both his first home and first away Tests. Suthar has now matched Nisar's rare achievement.His performance in Galle also placed him alongside two of India's most successful Test spinners. By taking six wickets in the second innings, Suthar became only the third Indian to claim a six-wicket haul in a Test innings in Sri Lanka, following Ravichandran Ashwin and Harbhajan Singh.Suthar ended the match with outstanding figures of 10 for 131 from 54.2 overs. In the process, he broke Harbhajan's record for the best bowling figures by an Indian in a Test played in Sri Lanka.Harbhajan had taken 10 for 153 in Galle during the July-August 2008 Test.Suthar also became the youngest Indian to claim a 10-wicket haul in a Test match. He is now the third Indian after Harbhajan and Ashwin to take 10 wickets in a Test in Sri Lanka.However, the overall record for the best match figures by a visiting bowler in Sri Lanka remains with South Africa's Keshav Maharaj. The left-arm spinner took 12 for 283 against Sri Lanka in the July 2018 Test at the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo.At just 24, Suthar has already made his mark in several statistical record books, with his breakthrough performance in Galle adding another significant chapter to his young Test career.
Article Summary: Manav Suthar becomes the first spinner to take five wickets in both his first home and first away Tests. The 24-year-old took six wickets for 55 runs as India beat Sri Lanka by 165 runs in Galle. He also became the youngest Indian to claim a 10-wicket haul in a Test match. He is the third Indian after Ravichandran Ashwin and Harbhajan Singh to take 10 wickets.

Article Title: Pakistan to host England, Sri Lanka in six-match ODI Tri-Series

Pakistan will host England and Sri Lanka in a six-match ODI tri-series from October 18 to 31, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) announced on Wednesday.Matches will be played in Rawalpindi and Lahore, with the top two teams meeting in the October 31 final at Gaddafi Stadium.Pakistan will open the tournament against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi on October 18 before taking on England at the same venue two days later. Article Title: First in 43 years! Azan Awais matches unwanted Pakistan record in England Test
Article Text:
Azan Awais

Robinson joins select England list

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Picked the wicket on the first ball of the Test in England

Maurice Tate vs AUS, Leeds, 1926 (W Bardsley)

Geoff Arnold vs IND, Birmingham, 1974 (S Gavaskar)

Ryan Sidebottom vs WI, Chester-le-Street, 2007 (D Ganga)

Ollie Robinson vs PAK, Leeds, 2026 (Azan Awais)*

Robinson leads Pakistan top-order collapse

Pakistan opener Azan Awais was dismissed off the very first ball of the first Test against England at Headingley on Wednesday, becoming only the second Pakistani opener ever to suffer the unwanted fate.Ollie Robinson produced a superb delivery to trap Awais lbw with the opening ball of the three-match series. The right-arm seamer's wobble-seam delivery moved sharply into the left-hander and struck him in front of off stump. Awais played around the ball and was given out by umpire Chris Gaffaney.Pakistan reviewed the decision, but replays showed a clear gap between bat and ball, while ball-tracking indicated three reds with the delivery hitting the top of middle stump. Awais departed for 0 off one ball.The dismissal made Awais only the second Pakistan opener to be dismissed from the first delivery of a Test. The previous instance came in 1983, when Mohsin Khan was dismissed off the first ball against India in Jalandhar.Robinson's strike also made him only the fourth England bowler to take a wicket with the first ball of a Test played in England.Maurice Tate was the first to achieve the feat against Australia at Leeds in 1926, dismissing Warren Bardsley.Geoff Arnold then struck against India at Birmingham in 1974, removing Sunil Gavaskar, while Ryan Sidebottom dismissed Daren Ganga against West Indies at Chester-le-Street in 2007.Robinson became the latest entrant to the list by removing Awais at Headingley.The early breakthrough was also a dramatic start to Robinson's return to the England side. The seamer had last played a Test at Lord's against New Zealand in June, where he claimed match-winning figures of 7-77 in his first Test appearance in two years.Robinson continued to trouble Pakistan's top order as the opening session unfolded. He removed four of Pakistan's top five batters, helping England seize control after rain had shortened the morning session.Pakistan slipped to 150/7 by tea, with Robinson finishing the extended three-hour session with impressive figures of 4-39 from 16 overs.
Article Summary: Azan Awais dismissed off the first ball of the first Test at Headingley. Ollie Robinson took the wicket of the Pakistani opener. Awais is only the second Pakistan opener to be dismissed from the first delivery of a Test. The previous instance was Mohsin Khan against India in 1983.

Article Title: 'Tough when you don't play much Test cricket': Sri Lanka head coach Gary Kirsten after India loss
Article Text:
Indian player greet after winning the first Test cricket match between India and Sri Lanka, in Galle, Sri Lanka. (PTI Photo/Shailendra Bhojak)

Sri Lanka need to build a stronger Test side

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sri Lanka head coach Gary Kirsten has urged his team to turn the progress they have made through more Test cricket into actual results after India handed them a 165-run defeat in the first Test in Galle.The loss means Sri Lanka are still waiting for their first Test win since Kirsten took charge. They have lost two of their three Tests under the former South Africa batter, including a defeat against the West Indies in Antigua in June.Kirsten said a lack of regular Test cricket had made it difficult for his players to adapt to the demands of the format."It's sometimes tough when you don't play much Test cricket to understand how you need to play," Kirsten said after the loss.Sri Lanka were dismissed for 206 while chasing 372 in the final innings, with India's young spinner Manav Suthar taking six wickets for 55 runs and finishing with 10 wickets in the match.Kirsten said Sri Lanka needed a bowling attack capable of regularly taking 20 wickets if they wanted to compete consistently in Tests."You need to be able to get 20 wickets consistently, bowl teams out with your seam, and be able to bowl teams out with spin as well.It's really important that we develop that Test match squad," he said.Despite the defeat, Kirsten was encouraged by the team's progress and welcomed a busier Test schedule. Sri Lanka are set to play six more Tests over the next six months."I think the challenge for the modern players, especially in Sri Lanka, is you don't play much Test cricket," Kirsten said."At least now we've got another six to go within the next six months or so, so it's great to get into the Test match game a little bit and then to understand how to score runs and bat for long periods of time and have an influence on a game over a long period of time," he added.
Article Summary: Sri Lanka lost to India by 165 runs in the first Test in Galle. Sri Lanka are still waiting for their first Test win under Gary Kirsten. Kirsten said a lack of regular Test cricket had made it difficult for his players to adapt to the demands of the format.

Article Title: Watch: English singer Laura Wright performs Pakistan's national anthem ahead of 1st Test against England
Article Text:
English singer Laura Wright performs Pakistan's national anthem (Screengrabs)

Robinson puts Pakistan under pressure

English singer Laura Wright performed Pakistan’s national anthem before the first Test between England and Pakistan at Headingley on Wednesday, where Joe Root’s return as England captain began with a strong start for the hosts.England won the toss and elected to bowl first in overcast conditions, with Ollie Robinson making an immediate impact. The fast bowler dismissed Azan Awais lbw with the very first ball of the series. Awais reviewed the decision, but the original call was upheld.It was the first time in England that a wicket had fallen from the opening delivery of a Test series.Robinson then struck again, trapping Pakistan captain Shan Masood lbw for five. His second wicket left Pakistan struggling at 6-2 after just a few overs.Watch Laura Wright perform Pakistan’s national anthem:Robinson, who was part of England’s four-man pace attack, finished the rain-shortened session with figures of 2-12 from five overs. Imam-ul-Haq and Abdullah Shafique were at the crease when rain interrupted play, with Pakistan reaching 23-2 after 9.4 overs.Root’s return to the captaincy was also eventful. The former England skipper used two reviews during the opening session, but neither decision was overturned.Heavy rain arrived around 50 minutes into the session, forcing the players off and bringing forward the lunch break to 12:30 p.m. local time.Both teams had entered the series looking to improve their recent Test form. England had won only two of its previous 10 Tests, while Pakistan had managed two victories in its last seven.Pakistan had also been searching for its first Test series win in England since 1996.With play interrupted by rain, England had made the ideal start through Robinson, while Pakistan was left needing its middle order to rebuild the innings when play resumed.

Ollie Robinson makes an immediate impact, dismissing Azan Awais lbw with the very first ball of the series. England won the toss and elected to bowl first in overcast conditions.

Article Title: ‘Magnificent’ Manav Suthar can serve India for a long time, says Shubman Gill
Article Text:
India's captain Shubman Gill and Manav Suthar (ANI Photo)

Gill praises Padikkal's composure

Gill delighted after weather concerns

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India captain Shubman Gill hailed the "magnificent" Manav Suthar after the young left-arm spinner's 10-wicket match haul powered India to a 165-run victory over Sri Lanka in the first Test in Galle, saying the 24-year-old looks capable of serving Indian cricket for a long time.Suthar followed his 4/76 in the first innings with a superb 6/55 in the second to finish with match figures of 10/126. It was his second successive five-wicket haul in as many Tests and capped a memorable outing in which he became the youngest Indian to take a 10-wicket haul in an away Test."He has been bowling magnificently. Looks like a very promising guy and someone who can play for India for a long time," Gill said at the post-match presentation ceremony.Gill also reserved special praise for Devdutt Padikkal, who was named Player of the Match after making 167 in the first innings and following it with 44 in the second. Padikkal was drafted into the No. 3 position after Sai Sudharsan failed to recover from a big toe injury."He has magnificent to watch. Important to get hundreds but even after getting a hundred. He got a big one. Being in a competitive match and in a comfortable position…the way he batted and dominated in the second innings, was great to watch," Gill said.Padikkal finished the match with an aggregate of 211 runs and felt Sri Lanka's left-arm spinners did not pose a major challenge because the Galle surface offered limited assistance early in the game."It was a bit of a slowish wicket, was not providing a lot of bite, so left-handed batters were able to negate the left-arm spinners. In the end, it was all about who came out on top with their skillset," Padikkal said after receiving the Player of the Match award."The wicket had its natural wear and tear, was a good Test wicket. Turned a lot more from the third day onwards."The victory gave India 12 crucial World Test Championship points and lifted some pressure on the side, although they remain fifth in the standings with 53.33 percentage points. Australia, South Africa, New Zealand and Bangladesh occupy the top four positions.Gill, however, stressed that India's ultimate target remains the WTC final."That (WTC final) is the ultimate goal. Test wins do not come easy and this one is delightful," he said.The Indian captain admitted there had been uncertainty over whether weather would allow the Test to reach a conclusion, with rain arriving soon after India completed victory."It is a very satisfying win for us. We were in a comfortable position, but were not sure if the match would go on (because of the weather), but the team responded well."Gill was also unfazed by India's second-innings collapse to 193 as the visitors looked to set up a declaration-style target quickly."Not really (bothered). We wanted to get (a lead) around 400 in the third innings. Wicket was not easy to score runs at will, so were looking to play more aggressively. We were unsure as to how many overs we would be able to bowl on days four and five. In that process, we lost a few wickets but we were still in a comfortable position."
Article Summary: India captain Shubman Gill hails Manav Suthar's 10-wicket match haul in first Test. India beat Sri Lanka by 165 runs to win the first Test in Galle. Devdutt Padikkal was named Player of the Match after making 167 in the first innings.

Article Title: 'Every Test match victory is special': India's vice-captain KL Rahul after 165-run victory in Galle Test
Article Text:
India's KL Rahul plays a shot on day four of the first test cricket match between India and Sri Lanka, in Galle, Sri Lanka. (PTI Photo/Shailendra Bhojak)

Confidence against spin

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Rahul praises Padikkal

India vice-captain KL Rahul was pleased with the team’s convincing 165-run win over Sri Lanka in the first Test, saying the result has boosted their confidence in handling spin-friendly conditions.India dominated across five days to take a 1-0 lead, with the second Test scheduled in Colombo from August 23.“I wouldn't say sigh of relief, just happy because every Test match victory is special. Coming back to Sri Lanka after a long time, so, lot of the guys haven't been here and so it's a great start to the tour. I think we ticked most of the boxes that we spoke about before the Test,” Rahul said.India had recently struggled against spin at home, but showed much better control against Sri Lanka’s spinners. Rahul believes the win will help the team ahead of the next Test and future challenges, including a major home series against Australia.“I think this victory will obviously give a sense of happiness and also give us the confidence going into the next game (at Colombo) and also we have a big home series coming up in India next year (vs Australia).“So just understanding batting against spin and playing in spinning conditions is something that we've all been working on.So from that point of view, it gives us a lot of happiness,” he added.Rahul said careful preparation played an important role in his own performance. He studied previous Sri Lanka matches and worked on when to attack, defend and handle pressure.“I've always liked doing that and taking those walks is a big part of my preparation. Yes, not always will you get success, but I think that’s the bare minimum someone playing at this level can do before coming for a Test series,” he said.Rahul also praised Karnataka teammate Devdutt Padikkal for his maiden Test century, calling it a key moment in India’s victory.“I think that innings was, I think for me, the defining part"of this Test match. The tempo that he batted with and to go on and get a big 100 in the first innings really set up the game for us.”Rahul hopes Padikkal can carry that confidence into the next Test and the rest of his career.
Article Summary: KL Rahul pleased with India's 165-run win over Sri Lanka in first Test. India vice-captain says result has boosted their confidence in handling spin-friendly conditions. Rahul praises Karnataka teammate Devdutt Padikkal for maiden Test century.

Article Title: ICC Test rankings: Harry Brook reclaims No.1 as Jasprit Bumrah retains top spot
Article Text:
Harry Brook and Jasprit Bumrah

Brook back on top, Bangladesh stars rise

Bumrah stays No. 1 despite Galle absence

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Harry Brook has reclaimed the No. 1 position in the ICC Men’s Test Batting Rankings, while India pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah retained his place at the summit of the bowling chart despite missing the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle.Brook returned to the top for the fourth time in his career after Australia opener Travis Head slipped three places to fourth following a disappointing outing in the opening Test of the two-match World Test Championship series against Bangladesh.Head managed scores of 22 and 17 as Bangladesh secured a memorable nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin. The result triggered significant movement at the top of the batting rankings, with England’s Brook moving back to No. 1, followed by teammate Joe Root at second and Australia veteran Steve Smith at third.Smith's scores of 71 and 44 in Darwin helped him leapfrog Head and move into third place.Brook first reached the No. 1 ranking in December 2024 and this marks his fourth stint at the top. With only 33 rating points separating the top four batters, the battle for the summit could remain tight in the coming weeks, with England set to host Pakistan and Australia facing Bangladesh in the second Test.Bangladesh's historic victory also brought significant rewards for several of their players.Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto climbed nine places to a career-best 20th after his crucial 84 in the first innings helped set up Bangladesh's victory. His 659 rating points are now the sixth-highest tally achieved by a Bangladeshi batter.Mominul Haque rose five places to 31st, while Australia all-rounder Cameron Green also moved up five spots to 30th after scoring a century in the second innings. Shadman Islam climbed three places to 58th, Mehidy Hasan Miraz moved five places to 59th and Tanzid Hasan made the biggest jump, rising 84 places to joint-88th.The bowling rankings also reflected Bangladesh's impressive performance. Mehidy moved three places to 24th after taking five wickets for 66 runs in Australia's second innings, while Hasan Mahmud jumped 26 places to 38th following his Player of the Match performance.Mahmud claimed six for 55 in the first innings and finished with nine wickets in the match.Despite sitting out India's first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle, Bumrah remains the world's top-ranked Test bowler.The India quick's position at the summit was unaffected by his absence, underlining the strength of his performances across the current rankings cycle. Bangladesh's strong showing in Darwin, meanwhile, allowed their bowlers to make notable gains behind him.There was also movement in the ODI rankings following Afghanistan's dominant 4-0 series victory over Ireland.Afghanistan captain Rashid Khan strengthened his position as the world's No. 1 ODI bowler after taking 12 wickets across the five-match series. Article Summary: Harry Brook has reclaimed the No. 1 position in the ICC Men’s Test Batting Rankings. Article Title: Galle conquered, boxes ticked: India’s Test blueprint takes shape
Article Text:

India head coach Gautam Gambhir was beaming with a smile as he descended the staircase from the Mahinda Rajapaksa Pavilion after India's emphatic 165-run win over Sri Lanka in Galle. With the shining Kookaburra in hand, Gambhir walked over to the opposition's side to exchange customary handshakes with the players and support staff led by former India coach Gary Kirsten. This wasn't the first encounter between the two in the last week, and it certainly won't be the last as the caravan moves soon to Colombo for the second Test.Both Gambhir and Kirsten are fighting their own challenges regarding Test cricket as head coaches. The hot seat feels hotter when the results don't go your way, and Gambhir has been feeling the heat since the whitewashes against New Zealand and South Africa at home and the away defeat against Australia in the Border-Gavaskar Trophy (BGT). India didn't qualify for the World Test Championship (WTC) final last edition and will need a special effort to turn it around in the ongoing cycle. Consequently, questions about Gambhir's methods in the format have only grown louder.The head coach has had to oversee tricky transitions, tackle workload issues and navigate injury concerns to assemble a multi-day squad that can serve the country for at least the next five years. While the results have hardly gone their way, the win in Galle not only ticked the crucial boxes but also firmed up the make-up of India's Test squad.They finally have a No. 3 who has the potential to provide the volume expected from that position. In Manav Suthar, there is an all-weather finger spinner for life after Ravindra Jadeja and beyond, while the pace battery is breathing fire with a much-improved Prasidh Krishna. The sample size isn't big enough to put your feet up and relax, but the signs are encouraging enough to be quietly confident about what lies ahead. And not to forget that the squad still misses plenty of first-choice selections due to injury concerns.Jasprit Bumrah was missing, but his absence wasn't felt. India didn't have the all-rounders Nitish Kumar Reddy and Washington Sundar, but their absence was not a concern. The regular No. 3, Sai Sudharsan, didn't recover in time to take the field, but a red-hot Padikkal was waiting in the wings and he caught the opportunity with both hands. So was Dhruv Jurel, who finally converted his 'A' consistency into a meaningful contribution with the bat. Prasidh Krishna is emerging as the biggest positive for the Shubman Gill-led unit and is showing why he continues to enjoy the captain's vote ahead of the exciting Gurnoor Brar.When vice-captain KL Rahul was asked about the win in the opener, he praised the group effusively and highlighted how ticking most boxes will give confidence going into the next Test, starting August 23 at the Sinhalese Sports Club (SSC) ground in Colombo."Very happy, every Test win is special. Great start to the tour, we ticked most of the boxes and did most things right. This victory will give a sense of happiness, and confidence before home series next year," Rahul told reporters in the post-match presser.Away from the strategies and intense discussions, one meet-up attracted a lot of attention. Every time Gambhir and Kirsten ran into each other, the shutterbugs were out with their cameras, capturing the frame featuring the individuals who played a key role in India's 2011 World Cup triumph. The roles had changed, but cricket, specifically coaching, dominated the conversation.The former India coach revealed how they both value Test cricket and how their efforts are directed at seeing their respective teams play the format in a certain way. The meet-ups didn't reminisce about the days gone by but focused on what lies ahead.“We didn't do much reminiscing. We actually spoke about coaching and the challenges of coaching. We both have very strong values around Test cricket, so we had good conversation around that, obviously trying to help our players play the best Test cricket that they can, both countries. So we spoke about that, and I think we have very similar ideas to how we want our teams to play Test cricket. So, yeah, we had good conversation around that,” said Kirsten at the post-match presser.Kirsten highlighted the positives for his team even after the defeat. His take on Test cricket, the squad and how to approach the format seemed pretty appropriate for the situation India found themselves in not long ago. There has been a lot of chatter around transitions, multiple retirements, combinations and captaincy changes, but all that is now a thing of the past and the team can finally focus on taking the required strides towards a WTC final berth.In the veteran coach's words, Test cricket is all about building some shape into the team and then "turn it into a performance".India have been taking shape since the BGT in 2024-25, found some performances in England, but the rude shock against South Africa at home derailed the train that was showing signs of heading in the right direction. When wins are hard to come by, the questions don't stop. They just keep getting louder.Both Gambhir and Kirsten are not sailing in the same boat regarding their respective coaching careers. However, taking a leaf from the South African's book on approaching Test cricket will definitely hold his Indian counterpart in good shape as he navigates the biggest challenge of his coaching career.
Article Summary: India beat Sri Lanka by 165 runs in the first Test in Galle. Gautam Gambhir's side will now face Sri Lanka in the second Test in Colombo. India captain KL Rahul praised the group and highlighted how ticking boxes will give confidence going into next Test.

Article Title: Rajasthan stuck in 2012, Manipur in 2023: How actively are states with CWG medals promoting sports?
Article Text:
Are sports bodies of Indian states promoting the game properly?

Haryana: Hit on the podium, not so much off it

Manipur still talking about 2023

And then come Tamil Nadu and others

The ones somewhere in the middle

How active are states/UTs with CWG medallists in promoting sport

Does it matter so much?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Social media presence Local sports events Government funding 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as she had watched on television just days ago. Her sole aim is to pull off the one like Sharmila Dhankar, India's Commonwealth Games shot put gold medallist.Before the 2026 CWG campaign, she, like many of us, had almost certainly never heard the name. And it's not because Dhankar had not won anything before the Glasgow Games; she had, a gold medal in the Women's Shot Put F57 event at the 2026 Fazza International Para Athletics Championship, but because one of the primary institutions whose entire job was to carry that story back from the medal podium to villages and training grounds across the state has, for all practical purposes, gone quiet.That's the part of this story that rarely gets told. India walked away from Glasgow with 39 medals, and for a week, the athletes who won them were everywhere, garlanded at airports, seated beside ministers, their faces on the evening news. But medals don't build the next generation of athletes by themselves. Somebody has to keep telling their stories, long after the felicitation photo is filed away, to the kid training in a dusty school ground who needs proof that this path actually leads somewhere.We wanted to know which state sports departments are still doing their job of promoting the sports and their grassroots on their social media platforms, and which ones seem to have simply logged off. So we scrolled through the timelines ourselves. Here's what we found.No state produced more glory in Glasgow than Haryana. Eleven medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze, spanning boxing, wrestling, athletics, and para sport, headlined by a Neeraj Chopra silver that will be replayed on sports channels for years.Alongside him were names most of India still had little knowledge of. The likes of Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, and Ankush Panghal, all of whom trained in government facilities, under government schemes, and who'd probably appreciate their own state department cheering as loudly for them as it does for its concert lineups.Because that's the thing. The Sports Department, Government of Haryana's X account has posted exactly once in all of 2026, and it's a flyer for the music acts playing at the Chief Minister's Cup.Facebook and Instagram follow a similar rhythm with a short cluster of posts around that February event, and then not much else.Eleven medals, and not one dedicated post to show for it. Somewhere in Rohtak or Bhiwani, a young pugilist training in Priya Ghanghas's discipline would probably just like a little proof that someone up top is paying attention.Manipur's page has an odd time-capsule quality to it. This is the state that gave India Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's most beloved Olympic medalists, and this Commonwealth Games alone produced four medalists from Manipur, Chanu's gold among them, alongside Rishikanta Singh, Bindyarani Devi, and Jadumani Singh.And yet the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports' X account hasn't posted since October 2023, a "Run for Unity" event, frozen well before any of this year's medals happened.Although the Facebook page has had a few sporadic posts here and there this year, its Instagram account has managed just two posts since January. It’s the kind of gap that makes you wonder if someone simply forgot the login details somewhere along the way.If there's one number in this whole exercise worth sitting with, it's this: the official Sports Department, Government of Rajasthan hasn't posted on Facebook since April 14, 2012.Fourteen years, through Arundhati Choudhary's Commonwealth gold and everything else that's happened in Rajasthan sport since.Its X account's last original post predates a retweet from March 2021, and there's no Instagram at all. A parallel handle, the Rajasthan State Sports Council, exists across all three platforms and is barely livelier.Somewhere behind Choudhary's medal is a genuinely good story, but it just hasn't found a home on the one page built to tell it.Gulveer Singh managed both a silver and a bronze for Uttar Pradesh this Games, a rare double that would make a great centrepiece for the state's sporting year. Instead, across two separate official handles on three platforms, Uttar Pradesh Sports has produced little beyond reposts, while its sister account, Sports Directorate, Govt of Uttar Pradesh, hasn't posted at all in 2026.Delhi Government, for its part, doesn't run a dedicated sports account at all on any of the popular social media platforms, so gold medalist Harsh Singh and bronze medalist Tejaswin Shankar, both representing India's capital, don't really have an institutional cheerleader online, their wins quietly absorbed into the general churn of city government updates. Both athletes are, in effect, doing their own promotional legwork.Set against all that quiet, Tamil Nadu feels like a different sport altogether. Its Sports Tamil Nadu handles post multiple times a day, celebrating not just its own three medalists, Praveen Chithravel, Selva Prabhu, Muthupandi Raja, but athletes from other states too, weaving in government scheme updates without it ever reading like bureaucracy.Every medallist got a dedicated post. Somewhere in Tamil Nadu, a kid training in long jump or wrestling doesn't have to wonder whether the sport leads anywhere. The state tells them, publicly, almost daily.Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka's Facebook and Instagram pages, Assam, Bihar, and Tripura all follow a version of that same habit, active, consistent, generous with attention toward athletes nobody outside their district would otherwise know existed.Kerala doesn't run a separate sports handle on X but keeps its Facebook and Instagram genuinely lively, making sure Murali Sreeshankar and Mohammed Basil's silvers got their due.Andhra Pradesh mirrors that same rhythm across all three platforms.Not every state falls neatly into being inactive or staying proactive. Punjab's account managed just two posts on X all year, New Year's and Republic Day, though its Facebook and Instagram carry a bit more life around coaching and departmental meetings, even if athletes rarely get top billing.Uttarakhand was genuinely active last year before cooling off in 2026, leaning more toward government scheme announcements on Facebook, though its Instagram at least carried two posts around the Games.Maharashtra has dedicated posts up for both Sarvesh Kushare and Dilip Gavit, with Instagram staying fairly regular, enough effort to stay out of the quiet column.Karnataka's X account hasn't posted since March 2024, around an unrelated cultural-team event, even though its Facebook and Instagram have stayed warm and active toward its CWG medalists.It is worth asking why this actually matters, beyond good manners. Well, a state sports department's social media feed isn't just a courtesy board for congratulations; it's one of the cheapest, most direct tools available to build the next generation of athletes.A youngster in a small town is far more likely to pick up a javelin because they saw a state government post celebrating someone from their own district. Even when it comes to promoting any government policy, social media can be as effective.Visibility drives aspiration. There's a funding logic too. Sponsors, corporates, and even state finance departments allocate resources partly based on visible public interest, and a well-run social account is often the easiest evidence a sport has that interest.ALSO READ: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensation Silence, on the other hand, sends the message that grassroots sport isn't a priority worth the effort of a single post, even when the state has just produced a medallist on the world stage.It is worth it because sometimes, the first step towards building a sporting culture is simply showing people that their achievements are being seen.
Article Summary: India won 39 medals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Haryana produced 11 medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze. But the state sports department has posted just once in all of 2026. What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Government funding or social media presence? Share your view.

Article Title: ‘That video was not ordinary’: PM Modi praises Lovlina for objecting to distorted India map - Watch
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi shares a light moment with boxer Lovlina Borgohain. (PTI Photo)

‘That video was not ordinary’

Mirabai opens up about four difficult years

Narender's joke leaves Modi laughing
